comparison: Both evaluations agree on ISRIB's potency (C2, C17, C54). OpenEval notes acceptable Z' factor and IC50 measurements with controls, while peer reviewers praised the 'remarkable potency' and thorough functional characterization. Full agreement on compound potency claims.

Both agree on ISRIB's specificity as ISR inhibitor. OpenEval cites Western blots and RT-PCR data (C18-C20) showing selective PERK pathway inhibition. Peer reviewers accepted the functional characterization showing ISRIB acts between phosphorylated eIF2α and downstream targets, also acknowledging multi-kinase activity (C32-C33). Strong agreement on specificity.

Both support mechanistic claims about ISRIB acting downstream of eIF2α phosphorylation. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from phospho-eIF2α measurements, metabolic labeling, and polysome analysis (C21-C26). Peer reviewers found functional characterization 'rather thorough' and accepted these mechanistic findings along with specificity controls (C27-C31).

OpenEval supports specificity controls using phosphomimetic mutant and alternative inhibitors (C27-C31). Peer reviewers grouped these with broader mechanistic characterization and accepted the thorough functional documentation. Agreement on experimental rigor of specificity controls.

Both agree ISRIB functions downstream of multiple eIF2α kinases (C32-C33). OpenEval cites amino acid starvation and HRI activator experiments. Peer reviewers explicitly noted ISRIB 'interposes itself between phosphorylated eIF2α and the target' without challenging multi-kinase activity. Full agreement.

Both support claims about ISRIB blocking ATF4-dependent gene induction (C35). OpenEval cites qRT-PCR data showing inhibition of CHOP and GADD34. Peer reviewers accepted this as part of thorough functional characterization without raising concerns.

Both support cellular stress response findings (C36-C41, C55-C56). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from survival assays, caspase activation, and UPR sensor imaging. Peer reviewers implicitly endorsed these findings through positive assessment of functional work. Strong agreement on cell viability and stress response data.

Disagreement on BBB penetration and lack of toxicity (C57). OpenEval finds pharmacokinetic data and behavioral studies sufficient to support CNS penetration and tolerability. Peer reviewers explicitly requested additional evidence of CNS penetration (CSF analysis or functional ISR measurements), indicating existing data was insufficient.

Disagreement on spatial learning enhancement claims (C45-C47). OpenEval finds Morris water maze data with multiple convergent measures sufficient. Peer reviewers were 'impressed' but raised concerns about CNS penetration evidence and differential treatment timing effects on consolidation conclusions, indicating uncertainty.

Disagreement on temporal selectivity of memory enhancement (C48-C50). OpenEval supports selective long-term memory effects as evidence for consolidation specificity. Peer reviewers questioned how differential treatment timing (chronic vs. post-training) affects consolidation conclusions, indicating uncertainty.

Disagreement on fear conditioning memory enhancement (C51-C52). OpenEval finds evidence from amygdala-dependent memory with local administration convincing. Peer reviewers' concerns about CNS penetration and treatment timing interpretation extend to these claims, indicating uncertainty.

Disagreement on mechanistic interpretation that ISR limits memory consolidation (C4, C5, C44, C53, C58). OpenEval finds converging evidence across paradigms and consistency with genetic models sufficient. Peer reviewers requested clarification on brain vs. peripheral action and treatment timing effects, indicating uncertainty about the mechanistic conclusion.

Partial overlap on C5 (ISR limits memory consolidation). OpenEval supports this interpretation based on behavioral data convergence. Peer reviewers' request to clarify brain vs. peripheral action suggests uncertainty about whether ISR specifically limits memory consolidation in the brain.

Agreement on uncertainty about molecular mechanism (C60, C62, C63). OpenEval notes claims are explicitly speculative with no direct target evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly stated molecular detail doesn't match functional characterization and requested co-IP experiments and phosphorylation analysis. Both agree mechanism remains uncertain.

Disagreement on cancer therapeutic potential (C66-C70). OpenEval considers therapeutic claims speculative without experimental cancer model data, despite mechanistic rationale. Peer reviewers accepted these discussion points without challenge, implicitly supporting the potential applications. OpenEval more conservative.

Disagreement on therapeutic speculation and evolutionary interpretation (C79-C81, C83-C84). OpenEval considers extrapolation to disease treatment and long-term safety speculative beyond experimental evidence. Peer reviewers accepted these discussion points, stating 'there is reason to hope that ISRIB will be applied to much further research.' OpenEval more conservative on speculative claims.
Minor overlap on C16 (screening metrics). Both evaluations support the screening methodology as part of thorough functional characterization. No disagreement.
Minor overlap on C34 (established knowledge about ATF4-dependent gene induction). Both accept this as established background information. No disagreement.
Minor overlap on C36 (established knowledge about ER stress and apoptosis). Both accept this as established background. No disagreement.
